Osotouy (historical Quapaw village)

Osotouy was a historical Quapaw village in what is now eastern Arkansas. The Arkansas Archeological Survey and National Park Service describe it in connection with the founding of the first French Arkansas Post in 1686.

Names & relationships

The NPS explicitly identifies Osotouy as a Quapaw village and places the first Arkansas Post there in 1686. The post later relocated. This does not identify a separate current government, a present boundary or the exact camera location of a modern landscape photograph.

Selected reading

01

Osotouy and early Arkansas Post

The Arkansas Archeological Survey describes Osotouy as a historical village in eastern Arkansas near the lower Arkansas River. The National Park Service study explains that the first French Arkansas Post was established beside this Quapaw settlement in 1686. The photograph shows the river landscape at the modern memorial.
